proposals.name: 1. Somerset lane with Quetelet strata (status-only review and adoption; draw by evidence class)
proposals.kind: route change + small tool change + Bentham strata
proposals.causes_addressed: route_or_tool_defect (valid status decision stranded when the lifecycle sheet is blocked: EO 12072, 13024, 11360, 11575, 14036, 14072, 10350, 13204, 10771); rule_too_strict ('bound means block', tools/prompts/producer.txt:19; exact first end per clause, assemble.py:552-556); lifecycle loss (Papinian 16 statuses accepted, 6 adopted; Haloander 6 accepted, 3 adopted); Bentham pricing the whole pool at one 0.10 rate.
proposals.design: (a) Route: any STATUS_DECISION.json that passes status_overlay._decision_errors goes to the independent status reviewer and then to adoption whether or not a lifecycle sheet exists. jobs/claim-kit/kit.py:200 already makes --lifecycle-sheet optional for overlay-propose; the change is in the wave tooling (research/excavator/claude-papinian-2026-11-10/tools/overlay_review.py and finish_pair.py forward only members with a submitted sheet) and in route_undecided.txt, which should tell the producer to file the status decision first and the lifecycle sheet second. The lifecycle claim stays a separate, later step with its two blind arms; nothing about it is relaxed. (b) Controls for a status-only batch: planted status controls (wrong actor, partial revocation presented as whole, savings clause removed) in each reviewer batch, as Sinclair and Jacquard did. (c) Quetelet strata: split status_assignment.undecided in jobs/bentham into machine-defined evidence classes computed from jobs/claim-kit/output (ACTING_PROVISIONS, OWN_TERMS, STATUS_LEADS, OVERLAY_INPUTS) and jobs/current-law/output/MENTIONS.csv, each with its own filed_per_attempt rate: S1 named whole-scope ending ACT on an acceptable original; S2 same plus concordant U.S. Code ended-status note; S3 printed U.S. Code note or eCFR text with no ending signal (needs proposal 4); S4 own-text end (needs proposal 3); S5 no ACT, TERM or current lead (4,174 orders: do not draw until a source job reaches them); S6 parked fact-date families (one-person waivers, land orders without a current record). jobs/bentham/measure.py:389-397 must also read the Papinian folder (no DISPOSITION.json with undecided_measure there today), so the 90-order sample enters the rate. (d) For S1/S2 a script pre-fills the decision's basis ids and quotes from the ACT record; the producer still confirms earlier ends, partial scope and savings (the six producer flags at status_overlay.py:647-650) and the reviewer still reads the held actor text. No status is machine-assigned.
proposals.files_to_change: research/excavator/<wave>/tools/overlay_review.py, finish_pair.py, prompts/route_undecided.txt, prompts/producer.txt:19; jobs/bentham/measure.py:389-422 and strata builder; jobs/claim-kit/completion.py:304-308 only if a status-only proposal needs its own publication mode (today working_overlay requires replacement_proposal).
proposals.orders_unlocked_estimate: Measured this session on origin/main claim-kit output (generation 2026-11-10T10:36Z): 687 undecided orders have a later held provision that names them with a whole-scope revoke/supersede/terminate/abolish/rescind verb, no savings phrase, not reached through a parent, AND an acceptable original (652 of them owe no page check); 240 of the 687 also carry a U.S. Code 'was revoked/superseded' note. Status-review acceptance on this route so far is 22 of 24 (Papinian 16/17, Haloander 6/7). Projection: about 550 to 630 NO statuses from S1 alone, against 6 per 90 drawn today. In the diagnosed samples the lane would have delivered at least 9 further reviewed statuses from 90 Papinian orders plus the 10 accepted-but-unadopted ones. These ACT counts are machine leads (upper bounds on eligibility, not on truth).
proposals.cost_estimate: Code: prompt and tooling edits, under one session. Run: Papinian measured $46.23 for 90 orders through producer, status reviewer and two lifecycle arms ($0.51 per drawn order, $7.70 per adopted status). Dropping the lifecycle arms for the status step and drawing only S1 should cost roughly $0.25 to $0.35 per order (estimate, not measured), i.e. about $170 to $240 for 687 orders, or roughly 2.5 to 3.5 statuses per dollar versus 0.13 today.
proposals.needs_owner_decision: Yes, one: may a status be adopted on this route from an accepted independent status review with planted controls, without waiting for a both-arms-upheld lifecycle claim? Precedent exists (Bowditch 15, Sinclair 29, Jacquard individual 888 were all status-only) but the three overlay-route adoptions (Dorotheus, Haloander, Papinian) each used the both-arms standard and a named decision.
proposals.risks: A status-only NO can hide a partial-scope or savings error that the lifecycle arms would have caught (EO 9680 shows the status reviewer does catch wind-up clauses; EO 10816 shows a reviewer side remark can be wrong). Three planted controls is all the evidence there is for reviewer sensitivity on this route, so the first status-only batches need more controls than one per batch. Machine pre-fill invites rubber-stamping; keep the pre-fill to ids and quotes, never the yes/no. Frozen evidence goes stale on every adoption merge (status_overlay.py:559-571 pins whole-file hashes), so batches must complete before the next adoption or the pin must narrow to the member's own rows.

proposals.name: 2. Bentley gate (apply the 2026-10-21 working-text ruling on the overlay route) and consume passed page checks
proposals.kind: tool fix (owner decision already on the books, not yet carried out)
proposals.causes_addressed: rule_too_strict: status_overlay.py:691-693 acceptable_original_required_for_status_proposal (EO 3761, 2145, 4041, 341A, 2738, 8965, 9013, 7778); :694-695 page check with no way to satisfy it (EO 7573, 7729, 8634, 8332, 11905); dispatch choosing a custody-only mirror over a held official printing (EO 4770, 5094, 5495, 9013).
proposals.design: (a) status_overlay.py:691-693: accept the selected text when acceptable_as_original is true OR the frozen evidence carries a valid working_text_confirmation (the overlay evidence already carries it, status_overlay.py:320-322, and working_text.py validates it) OR the grade is one the tracker already credits as original_supported (official_printing, government_printed_copy, machine_read_government_printed_copy, archival_replica_checked). In the second and third cases the proposal must carry the working-text disclosure string and the adoption row a flag 'status on disclosed working text', exactly as the 888 Jacquard adoptions did. (b) :694-695: treat a passed Montfaucon check as satisfying the page requirement: claim-kit reads jobs/montfaucon-page-check/output/FRAGMENTS_OFFICIAL.jsonl (needs_page_check false) and research/montfaucon/checks/*.jsonl when selecting the ORIGINAL, clears requires_page_check on a pass, and on a 'fail' with actual_pdf_pages re-points the span (EO 8332). (c) Text selection: prefer a held official_printing (jobs/photius-gpo-volumes, Mabillon) over a custody-only mirror or transcription before dispatch; run the owed Photius recheck (D-20261108-photius-recheck, not wired). (d) working_text.py:398-407: raise official_copy_available_recheck_required only when the held official copy actually contains the quoted span (EO 10350: the official extraction stops two pages before the revoking section).
proposals.files_to_change: jobs/claim-kit/status_overlay.py:691-695; jobs/claim-kit/working_text.py:398-407; jobs/claim-kit/build.py:187-196 (ORIGINAL selection and requires_page_check); jobs/claim-kit/inputs.txt (add montfaucon and photius outputs); tools/prompts/route_undecided.txt (remove the 'block transcription members' instruction).
proposals.orders_unlocked_estimate: Measured: 5,995 of 10,691 undecided have a selected text the gate refuses and 57 have none; 4,325 of the refused are texts the tracker already counts as original_supported. Immediately eligible once the gate opens: 369 refused-text orders with a whole-scope ending ACT (join stratum S1 of proposal 1), 2,743 with some ACT, TERM or current lead, and 1,972 of Pothier's 2,139 decided leads. Page checks: 198 acceptable undecided orders owe one (177 at EO 7532 or later). Sample evidence: 8 of 30 Haloander and 28 of 92 Dorotheus undecided orders were stopped by this gate alone; six of Haloander's fourteen pre-7532 failures are decidable NO today and fail only here.
proposals.cost_estimate: One coding session with tests (test_status_overlay.py, test_working_text_index.py). No fetch cost. Adds no per-order cost; it widens the pool the other proposals draw from.
proposals.needs_owner_decision: Confirmation only: D-20261021-transcriptions and the 2026-10-31 working-texts ruling already allow a disclosed working text; the owner should confirm that this extends to an overlay-route status proposal (no Kean ask exists to change the gate). Whether an adoption on a working text must be re-reviewed when the official original arrives is a second, smaller question.
proposals.risks: Pre-1936 transcriptions carry identity and OCR errors (Kappler gave EO 2225 a neighbour's TERM records; EO 341A's text is a War Department description, not the order). The disclosure keeps that visible but does not fix it, so identity confirmation by the reviewer must stay mandatory. Opening the gate without proposal 1's strata would pull thousands of leadless pre-7532 orders into expensive draws.

proposals.name: 3. Gaius records (own-text ending records and Pothier leads inside the dossier; amend-only and spent-on-issue classes extended past EO 7532)
proposals.kind: tool fix + machine job + producer prompt
proposals.causes_addressed: rule_too_strict at status_overlay.py:684-685 for self-executing, amend-only and own-term orders with own_terms [] (EO 7621, 5739, 12178, 12379, 10603, 13013, 13552, 12378); producer_error from the prompt not carrying ruling P2 (EO 11360, 10803, 10565, 14198, 8724, 12178); mistyped TERM kinds (EO 13064 and 13116 sunsets typed report_deadline, barred at status_overlay.py:678-679; EO 10565); Pothier leads never read by the kit.
proposals.design: No gate change is needed for NO: build.py:205-209 already turns every own-terms record into a TERM: id and line 684 accepts any TERM: id (the refuter confirmed EO 8724 and 10803 could have been proposed on the TERM id that quotes their operative sentence). The fix is to make the right record exist and be typed honestly. (a) Own-terms extractor (jobs/claim-kit/excavate.py and the clause-drafts upstream): new kinds spent_on_issue (every operative sentence is 'is hereby revoked/restored/terminated/abolished' with no continuing duty, EO 12379's 25 sections), amend_only_merged_into_parent (every operative sentence amends a named order; requires a parent pointer and records the parent text as the surviving consequence, per the owner's 2026-11-09 answer to A-20261106-pothier point 2), calendar_year_term ('during the current calendar year' plus signing year, EO 7573), enumerated_final_period ('for 1999, 2000, and 2001', EO 13116), stated_pause_until_date (EO 14198), abolished_as_of_date (EO 9680 sec. 1). Retype 'shall terminate no later than <date>' and 'may be retained no later than <date>' as sunset_date. Do NOT add the fiscal-year rule proposed for EO 8266: the refuter showed 'funds available during the fiscal years 1940 and 1941' qualifies the funds and states no end. (b) Pothier ingestion: a small job step writes each decided Pothier lead (jobs/pothier/output/LEADS.jsonl, basis TERM or ACT, with its matched span) into OWN_TERMS / act_overrides candidates so it appears in the frozen dossier as a machine lead with doctrine id and branch; it stays a lead that the producer and reviewer must confirm against the text. (c) Extend Pothier's P1/P2 text tests from the empty-history pool to every undecided order (the diagnosis shows none of the 90 Papinian orders was a Pothier member only because each had one catalog observation). (d) route_undecided.txt and producer.txt: add the command-type step first (self-executing act, amend-only, dated term, standing command) with the P2 wording, and the rule from 2026-10-28 point 1 that a reserved right or surviving text is recorded under savings, not as a material gap. (e) assemble.py:552-556: accept a first end 'by performance on signing' whose source is the order's own TERM record.
proposals.files_to_change: jobs/claim-kit/excavate.py (TERM patterns near lines 28-31 and the term kinds), jobs/clause-drafts (own-terms typing), jobs/claim-kit/build.py:205-209 (carry kind-specific mechanism), jobs/claim-kit/assemble.py:552-556, jobs/pothier (membership filter), jobs/claim-kit/inputs.txt, tools/prompts/route_undecided.txt and producer.txt.
proposals.orders_unlocked_estimate: Measured: Pothier holds 2,088 NO leads for undecided orders, of which 1,131 are own-text TERM leads of exactly these kinds (601 merged_into_parent_on_issue, 530 spent_on_issue); only 103 of those 1,131 sit on an acceptable original, so the rest also need proposal 2. Pothier pilot error was 1 of 129 decided leads (95% upper bound 4.2%). Past EO 7532, the OFR 1989 table marks 334 undecided orders as taking effect inside another document (270 amends, 36 revokes, 18 terminates, 10 modifies), a lower bound on the amend-only and spent classes there. Machine own-terms records with a dated non-deadline end before the cutoff exist for 556 undecided orders (259 on acceptable originals). In the samples these classes decide about 11 of 90 Papinian orders and 4 of 27 Haloander failures. Projection if reviewed one by one at Jacquard wave-2 rates (773 of 1,037 upheld): roughly 800 to 1,000 NO statuses from the 1,131 Pothier TERM leads plus 250 to 400 later orders.
proposals.cost_estimate: One to two coding sessions (extractor patterns with tests, Pothier membership, prompts). Run cost if taken through proposal 1's lane with reviewers only on a machine-built lead: Jacquard wave 2 measured about 8k Sonnet tokens per adopted status; with a producer in the loop about $0.25 to $0.35 per order (estimate).
proposals.needs_owner_decision: Three points. (1) The owner's 2026-11-09 answer made Pothier doctrines first-step guidance and left sampled adoption of a family's NO leads 'a later ask under the Jacquard rule'; individual review needs no new ruling, lot adoption does. (2) A rule for an incidental wind-up or liquidation direction attached to an abolition (EO 9680 sec. 2, EO 10917 sec. 2): today the 2026-10-28 ruling as applied by the status reviewer keeps the whole order open. (3) Whether P1 covers interdepartmental jurisdiction transfers, naming designations (EO 10828) and covering-in orders (EO 3330).
proposals.risks: A spent-on-issue pattern can miss a continuing duty elsewhere in the order (EO 11315 mixes amendments with a standing system; the ledger still carries amend-only EO 12043 as provisional YES, so the project is not yet uniform on P2). The amend-only record must never be read as deciding the parent. Machine typing errors already exist (ordinary sentences typed report_deadline); new kinds add new ways to mistype, so each needs a regression fixture from the diagnosed orders.

proposals.name: 4. Tribonian slices (CURRENT records from current-law text that is already held)
proposals.causes_addressed: The structural zero: no undecided dossier has a CURRENT: record, so YES is impossible (status_overlay.py:686-690; build.py:231-239). held_not_routed for EO 11225, 11866, 13505, 14233, 14318, 13647, 14051, 14191, 10624, 13329, 13748, 12661, 8695, 12214, 14238, 14348.
proposals.design: (a) jobs/current-law publishes every printed executive-order note as its own attributed UTF-8 text file (name by USLM note id; header with citation, member file and its sha256, release point), declared in jobs/current-law/output/SOURCES.jsonl with url, sha256, text_path and text_sha256, and points each FRAGMENTS lead at that file instead of 'USC_EO_NOTES.jsonl#note_id=...'. That satisfies current_evidence.py:17 (no '#'), :36-38 (declared in current-law SOURCES) and :77 (.txt) with no change to the kit's refusal to promote JSON. Fix the extractor that truncates notes organised in PARTs or articles (EO 13116: 875 characters; EO 12661: 1,244). Source: https://uscode.house.gov/download/releasepoints/us/pl/119/121/xml_uscAll@119-121.zip (public, free, already hashed). (b) Same for eCFR: retain the point-in-time section or part text for every CFR unit that names an order (8 CFR 316.20, 19 CFR 101.3, 5 CFR part 6, 15 CFR part 730) from https://www.ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/2026-10-14/title-N.xml (public, free), so the text is the cutoff-date text and not a later edition (the held 5 CFR 6.6 copy is dated 2026-11-05). (c) theophilus-sources: run for undecided orders with a current-law lead, and add a field cited_orders listing every order number printed in a fetched section; stop using instrument_ids as the identity of the text, which built 42 bogus ACT:EO:13329>EO:12333 records and ACT:EO:12661>EO:12261. (d) current_evidence.enrich_current: also read jobs/theophilus-sources/output/SOURCES.jsonl and jobs/source-ladder/output SOURCES declarations, matched by citation plus exact unique snippet. (e) Cutoff currency (status_overlay.py:689): the release point stops at 2026-10-09. Hold one shared 'cutoff window' record: the complete list of presidential documents published in the Federal Register from 2026-10-09 through 2026-10-14 (https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents.json with type PRESDOCU and the date range; public, free) so the five days are covered by a complete enumeration that the producer reads, not by silence. (f) Index the held OFR disposition-table capture of 2026-10-12 (source-ladder queue file ...fb92020005.txt) by every order it lists, as a dated editorial observation in status-history; it is a cross-check, never the basis. (g) Producer checklist for YES: read the order's own terms for an enumerated period or sunset before treating a printed note as current (EO 13116 is printed in the Code and ended in 2001); name the clause that still commands.
proposals.files_to_change: jobs/current-law (note and eCFR extract publication, SOURCES.jsonl, FRAGMENTS pointers); jobs/theophilus-sources (membership, cited_orders); jobs/claim-kit/current_evidence.py:35-38 and :60-77; jobs/claim-kit/build.py (ignore usc/cfr section sources as actor texts); jobs/status-history (disposition capture observations); tools/prompts/route_undecided.txt (YES checklist copied from route_yes.txt).
proposals.orders_unlocked_estimate: Measured from jobs/current-law/output/MENTIONS.csv on origin/main: 769 undecided orders are printed in the U.S. Code as notes (764 on acceptable originals); 734 of those have no whole-scope ending ACT and no ended-status note. 453 undecided orders are named in eCFR text (295 of them not printed in the Code). 893 acceptable-original undecided orders have at least one positive current source (printed note, eCFR text or statutory text) and no ending signal. By range the printed notes are 506 at EO 13000+, 238 at 10000-12999, 18 at 7532-9999. Sample: 13 of 90 Papinian and 3 of 30 Haloander orders were YES readings stopped only by this gate. YES acceptance by an independent reviewer on this route has never been measured (all 16 adoptions are NO), so the projection is wide: 450 to 700 YES statuses.
proposals.cost_estimate: One to two coding sessions; the job runs on GitHub Actions at no token cost. eCFR titles are tens of MB each; store per-section extracts only. Per-order producer and status reviewer about $0.30 to $0.50 (estimate; YES needs an own-terms read of the whole order).
proposals.needs_owner_decision: One: for an order with no code footprint whose own stated period runs past the cutoff and which is the last order in the census (EO 14435), may ORIGINAL plus a complete enumeration of later presidential documents serve as the current predicate, as the decided-YES route's original_plus_bounded_search does? I do not propose the general 'no named ending found' predicate suggested for EO 9794 and 13013: under D-20261028 that infers force from absence, and those orders stay unknown.
proposals.risks: A printed note shows the codifiers still print the text, not that every command still operates; unrevoked councils and spent report orders are printed too (EO 13748, 14223). A YES therefore needs a named continuing clause, and reviewers need planted YES controls (for example an order whose note carries a '[Revoked by ...]' bracket deeper in the text). CFR source credits attribute wording to an order that later amendments may have replaced (EO 11315). Unit-keyed predicates (a refuge or port named without the order number) are out of scope here.

proposals.name: 5. Accursius router (held later-event evidence reaches the frozen dossier; locator repairs)
proposals.causes_addressed: held_not_routed and locator defects: U.S. Code ended-status notes absent from the dossier (EO 13024, 10771, 10917, 11575, 12576, 10195, 11053, 11118); 'target provision not located' although the actor text is held (EO 13354, 11575, 11360, 7729, 3761, 10585); actor texts over 50,000 bytes get no evidence id (build.py:224-229, EO 13354); public land orders dropped as 'absent from census' (build.py:427: EO 8790, 8649); parent-level endings not routed to amenders (EO 14231, 14198, 12378, 13064); Selden statutes and Federal Register citers never consumed (EO 9372, 9211, 13204, 8104); pre-1936 replica texts never swept for citations (EO 2738).
proposals.design: (a) Notes as locators, not as endings: for each MENTIONS row of role eo_note_ended_status, ending_order_in_status_line or amending_order_in_ended_status_line, parse 'was revoked/superseded by Ex. Ord. No. N, § x ... [date, see FR cite]' and search actor N's held official text for the target's bare number; emit an ACT record from the actor's own text when found, and otherwise a candidate record for research/readiness/act_overrides (act_overrides.py already admits a reviewed agent-located record for a 'not located' pair). The note itself enters the dossier as a citable editorial cross-check. (b) excavate.py:23 EO_REF: enumerate list forms ('Executive Order Nos. 11526, 11575, 11662, and 11678'; 'Orders 13354 and 13355 ... are'; 'No. 3761, of December 6, 1922'), parse EO 12553's table of bare numbers, tolerate OCR in dates and footnote-fused numbers, and match 'designated as the date of termination ... described in Executive Order No. N'. (c) build.py:224-229: when an actor text overflows, still emit the located provision span as an ACT record with its own id, and add jobs/claim-kit/output/actor-texts to worktree sparse sets. (d) build.py:427: admit PLO identities (and proclamations 2416, 2439) as actors backed by jobs/selden-fr-acting/output/LOCATED.csv and texts, so a held land order becomes an ACT record. (e) Parent chain: for an order whose every operative sentence amends parent P, add to its dossier each later instrument that ends, suspends or supersedes P 'as amended' (build.py:415-421 already forms such pairs; extend it to acts located on the parent after the amender's date, and to FACA continuance lists), marked reaches_target_via so the reviewer confirms scope. (f) Freeze-time supplements, automated: route jobs/selden-statutes texts for the statutes an order's own terms name, and jobs/selden-fr-citers documents whose ACTION line and summary name the order, as SUPPLEMENT: evidence (source_supplement.py:73-218 reaches undecided dossiers since 48da66f755). They are citable for dates and performance; they are not an ending basis and I do not propose changing that. (g) Report every MENTIONS row in machine_searches (jobs/claim-drafts/drafts.py:1453-1455 counts fragments only, per the diagnosis; not re-read by me) and run Geddes citing-checks on overlay working claims. (h) Run the later-events citer over jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest and jobs/pinakes-htr texts. (i) Drop ACT leads whose span is another order's body or a whole FR issue (EO 8104's 46 junk records; inverted EO 12379 edges).

proposals.orders_unlocked_estimate: Measured: 344 undecided orders have a U.S. Code ended-status note; 74 of them have no whole-scope ending ACT at all (73 on acceptable originals). 210 undecided orders are amenders named in an ended status line; 164 of those have no whole-scope ACT (all on acceptable originals). So about 238 orders gain a named ending they lack today, on top of the 687 in proposal 1. 632 undecided orders already carry an ACT reached through a parent. Pothier holds 108 decided PLO-based leads; Selden's census counts 869 undecided orders with a named ending instrument not held as official text and 782 PLO texts supplied since. Projection: 250 to 450 further NO statuses, plus fewer lifecycle rejections for 'no hit' sentences (EO 10195, 12576).
proposals.cost_estimate: Two to three coding sessions; the largest item of tool work here. No fetch cost: every source named is already on origin/main. Act-override candidates need an independent reviewer each (about the cost of a status review).
proposals.needs_owner_decision: One: whether a held statute that repeals an order's sole authority and re-assigns or abolishes the function, without naming the order, can ground a NO under 2026-10-28 point 3 (EO 8490, 9372, 10803, 8099, 9211, 8875; D-20261021-unnamed-instruments and D-20261106-justinian-r3 point the other way; the 1961 Act's sec. 643(a) savings clause shows why it cannot be automatic). Until ruled, such statutes are routed and disclosed as earlier candidate ends only.
proposals.risks: The U.S. Code note is editorial and occasionally wrong (10 U.S.C. 2922c misprints 12261 as 12661; the OFR label for EO 8790 misreads PLO 3749), so it may only point to the operative text. Parent-chain propagation can over-attach (EO 8104's junk edges came from exactly that), so every propagated record needs the reaches_target_via flag and a scope confirmation. Federal Register citers include template errors and page-number false positives; they must be read, not counted.

proposals.name: 6. Panizzi custody (re-verifiable Federal Register bytes so held texts are citable)
proposals.causes_addressed: route_or_tool_defect: dispatch and completion grade custody_record_only when the text is committed and the PDF is public (EO 13411, 14223, 10603, 10917, 13820, 13836, 10955, 10472, 10350, 7778).
proposals.design: (a) Fetch-and-verify at check time: for a source whose url is a govinfo Federal Register issue or document PDF (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-YYYY-MM-DD/pdf/FR-YYYY-MM-DD.pdf or .../pdf/<docnumber>.pdf; public, free) and whose sha256 is recorded, a job re-downloads, compares the hash and writes a dated verification row; jobs/claim-kit/dispatch.py source_held (the blocker raised at dispatch.py:153-155) accepts 'verified re-fetch within N days' as held. No bytes enter git. (b) Where the owner wants bytes kept, use the Release-asset store chosen in D-20261110-papinian-board-bytes; resume Ptolemy only against that store (jobs/ptolemy-custody/PAUSED explains the 10 GB limit). (c) Run the custody check on producer-chosen ending and later-event sources before review, not at completion (EO 10955 was upheld by both arms and then refused), and show reviewers the dispatch check's unusable-source list (EO 10472).
proposals.files_to_change: jobs/claim-kit/dispatch.py:140-160; jobs/ptolemy-custody (store target, request builder to include FR issue PDFs); jobs/claim-checker source_held; reviewer prompt.
proposals.orders_unlocked_estimate: Measured: the draft checker marks the original of 1,361 of the 4,639 acceptable-original undecided orders custody_record_only (502 at EO 7532-9999, 390 at 10000-12999, 111 at 13000+, 358 below 7532). Only 111 of them (106 files, 0.10 GB) are in Ptolemy's request queue, so the paused backlog is not the main gap: the large FR issue PDFs are not queued at all. Observed block rates are lower than that flag suggests (Papinian 6 of 90 dispatch-blocked, Haloander 3 of 30 on pure custody plus one completion refusal), because dispatch accepts GPO hash matches; I did not reconcile the two measures. proposals.name: 7. Littleton checklist (producer and reviewer prompt items and pre-handback lints)
proposals.causes_addressed: producer_error (EO 11726, 12576, 10195, 10816, 12200, 11202, 11813, 10938, 10565, 8617, 9181, 9231, 14198, 14231, 13116, 8875); reviewer guidance conflict (EO 10816); missing after-reveal review (EO 11816); unreviewed genuine claims.
proposals.design: Producer (route_undecided.txt, producer.txt): 1 classify the command first (self-executing, amend-only, dated term or pause, standing); 2 read own terms for calendar years, enumerated periods and sunsets before anything else; 3 open every MENTIONS.csv row and every U.S. Code note naming the order or its office and answer each; 4 read every ACTOR_TEXT, every actor in the OFR note and the 1989 row before calling an instrument missing; 5 for an amending order search the parent's number; 6 search jobs/selden-statutes and jobs/selden-fr-citers before writing 'not held'; 7 an abolition that transfers functions is a continuation, name what extinguishes the command; 8 a reserved right or surviving text goes under savings; 9 take counts and page numbers off the sheet and the page header, never from memory; 10 use inventory_overrides when dispatch reports inventory_incomplete. Lints in overlay-check and batch-check: prose clause count equals len(operative_clauses); a first_end whose source contains 'in lieu thereof' or 'to read as follows' with a replacement mechanism is refused unless the parent ended that day; 'no hit' statements compared with recorded hits; rationale containing a date earlier than first_end or the words 'reviewer should' with empty material gaps is refused; a clause span containing a second section heading fails; apply refuses inventory_confirmed=true without overrides when dispatch flagged inventory_incomplete; a sheet whose chain holds an unrecorded amendment event is refused. Reviewer prompts (reviewer_overlay.txt, reviewer.txt): carry the strike-and-insert and report-deadline rulings; status reviewers give a verdict, not clause-level side advice. Every planted control gets an after-reveal review of the genuine version in the same wave. Schema: later_events gains before/after text and a reviewer-note field (assemble.py:590) so the strike-and-insert ruling can be met.

Producer 'not held' statements were wrong for 8 or more of 90 orders. If the lints catch what they are written for, lifecycle yield per accepted status roughly doubles; with proposal 1 in place this affects ready-for-review claims rather than the undecided count.
proposals.cost_estimate: Under one session for prompts; one session for lints with tests. Adds a few hundred tokens per producer prompt.
proposals.needs_owner_decision: None for the checklist. The later_events schema change touches research/stage19/CLAIM_SCHEMA.md and should be confirmed.

proposals.name: 9. Bede facts (reviewed shared fact set for wartime terminations and other own-term conditions)
proposals.kind: machine job (statute fetch) + small reviewed register + routing
proposals.causes_addressed: missing_later_event of kinds statute_not_held and nea_continuation_or_emergency_termination where the order's own terms name the condition (EO 9181, 9231, 9408, 8627, 9211, 7942, 1586); the assemble.py:552-556 exact-date rule for a reasoned bound.

The NO basis remains the order's own TERM id, which line 684 already accepts; the fact supplies the date. This applies only where the order's own text names the condition. Where a statute merely bounds the authority without being named in the order's terms (EO 9408, 9211), the bound is disclosed as a not-later-than candidate and the question goes to the owner. Catalog-index family sizes from the diagnosis: 26 eight-hour-law orders, about 69 plant-possession orders, 40 orders listed in EO 9521, the Public Resolution 96 induction orders. Items 2 to 4 would enter as a new evidence class UNIT_CURRENT: 'predicate names the unit, not the order', which under the present gate cannot support YES. A positive record that a later PLO revoked the remainder supports NO through item 1; a unit list by itself supports nothing until the owner rules.

Pool: the 1989 table marks 262 undecided orders 'public lands'; Pothier leaves 411 standing withdrawals and 194 national-forest orders open pending a record; the catalog index has about 70 refuge orders from 1937 on; Selden counted 902 unheld PLOs (782 since supplied). PLO texts alone should decide the fully revoked ones (Pothier already has 108 decided PLO leads); the standing ones stay open without the ruling. If the owner adopts a bounded-interval rule for waivers, on the order of 900 to 1,500 orders become decidable by rule; that number is the family size, not a yield.

design:standing-rule.summary:
Design for a standing adoption rule ("Respondendi", after the ius respondendi; the branch already carries the name) and the machinery to apply it. Read-only work; nothing was changed. Five proposals: the exact rule text, the safeguards, the owner-decision gate, the module and CLI, and reversal plus three small prerequisites.

Facts from the code that shape the design:
- **Both-arm rule is not in the kit.** `completion.py` pins only arm A per member (`member.review`); arm B is only a receipt, and the both-uphold rule lives in the wave's own `tools/overlay_review.py`. One `CONTROL_ADJUDICATION` covers both arms. The adopter must re-derive both arms from the pinned review files.
- **Planted claims are not committed.** The control seed receipt may hold only five keys, and the planted versions sit in a temp folder, so "the reviewer named the planted defect" is checkable today only by word matching (`dated()`).
- **No admission receipts for the adopted batches.** `admission.record` writes `ADMISSION.json`, but none exists under the Papinian wave folder (I did not check whether the wave predates `admission.py`), and the receipt pins neither the plan nor the order list.
- **Any ledger change stales frozen overlay evidence.** `status_overlay._authority_for` pins the whole ledger file's sha256, and `completion.working_overlay` re-pins it. The adopter therefore checks completed batches by their completion receipts plus a ledger-prefix test; it cannot re-run `validate_evidence`.
- **`population.py` is a compiler-pinned file.** Editing `validate_inputs` stales every frozen evidence and compiled output until a rebuild. Reversal is therefore designed to work with the current code.
- **Canonical claim files are append-only** (`publication_audit`), so a withdrawn adoption keeps its claim line and gets a source-audit hold.
- **A count-changing PR still needs an owner merge** (A-20261028-1, D-20261106-dorotheus-r13). The rule must carve this out or each batch still needs an owner action.
- **The adoption precedents for same-family review are narrow.** A-20261028-4 and D-20261031-claude-reviewers cover sampled class review only; D-20261106-dorotheus-r11 requires a named Kean decision before Codex reviews.

Measured basis: 9 adoptions from 120 attempted undecided orders (Haloander 3 of 30, Papinian 6 of 90), all NO, 5 of 5 controls caught by both arms... correction: 3 controls across the three review sets (EO 10955, 11816, 10938), all caught by both arms. Bentham's gate said STOP (0.12) on the undecided action after u23, so the rule pays off only as the route's yield rises.

proposals.design:
File: research/readiness/standing_rules/respondendi-v1.md. The sha256 of this file (LF bytes) is what the owner decision pins. The numbers live in a JSON block at the end of the same file, so one hash covers prose and parameters.

---
RESPONDENDI STANDING ADOPTION RULE, VERSION 1

Scope. This rule lets the claim kit adopt a provisional whole-order status for an order that has no ledger status, without a separate owner decision for that order, when every condition below is shown by files pinned by sha256 in the adoption record. It adopts provisional AI status hypotheses only. Every adopted row keeps human_certified_by_this_release = no, and the certified whole-lifecycle count stays 0. It changes no codebook text, census identity or owner ruling.

An order qualifies only if all of these hold.
1. Undecided and admitted. The order is in the census, has no row in the status ledger, and was prepared under a Bentham action in this rule's action list, shown by the packet's admission receipt and that action's order list.
2. Proposal. A status-overlay bundle (EVIDENCE, STATUS_DECISION, STATUS_REVIEW, PROMOTION_PROPOSAL) exists; the producer's decision and the review pass the kit's validators with no error; the sealed proposal matches them and recommends the status adopted.
3. Independent status review. STATUS_REVIEW records "accept" by a reviewer other than the producer, pinned to the exact decision and evidence, with independence and source checks confirmed.
4. Two blind arms. Two separate-context reviewers, different from the producer, the status reviewer and each other, each recorded "upheld" with no defects for the exact claim hash at scope whole_case ("upheld_after_reveal" for the genuine version of a control).
5. Control. The same two review files hold at least one planted control per 15 claims (at least one), seeded before review. Both arms rejected the exact planted hash and named a planted field. No control in the set was missed by either arm. The planted versions are committed after review.
6. Checker. The actual claim checker passed the exact claim in the completion run (mechanical pass, gate passed, all five steps, no completion exception) and passes it again on the filed claim.
7. Uncontested. No recorded review of any genuine version of the order's status decision or claim, in any wave, is a rejection. No source-audit hold is open on the claim. The claim's status equals the proposal's. The tracker lists no contest for the order.
8. Provenance. Every source cited by the claim and the frozen evidence still has its recorded sha256, and the ledger at adoption is the ledger the evidence was frozen against plus rows for other orders only.
9. Status. NO qualifies under clauses 1 to 8. YES qualifies only with a CURRENT record checked through 2026-10-14, and every YES is audited before adoption.

Safeguards.
10. Limits. At most 30 orders per batch, one batch per day, and 1,000 orders under this version.
11. Audit. Before a batch is adopted, a seeded random sample of it is audited blind by a reviewer of a different model family from the producer and reviewers, or by a human: every order until 59 audits in a row have agreed; after that one in five, at least two per batch; always every YES. The auditor applies the owner rulings of 2026-10-28 (evidence decides) and 2026-10-21 (unnamed instruments).
12. Stop. An audit disagreement, a missed control or a failed verification suspends this rule at once. The batch is not adopted and the disagreement goes to the owner as an ask. Only a new owner decision lifts a suspension, and the count of agreeing audits restarts at 0.
13. Reversal. An adoption is withdrawn when the owner says so, or when a later audit, review or source shows the status unsupported. Withdrawal removes the ledger row by a pinned withdrawal record. The original adoption rows, their evidence pins and the filed claim stay, the claim under a source-audit hold. The order returns to undecided.
14. Report. Each batch writes a report, the owner brief carries one standing line (adopted, audited, disagreements, withdrawn, upper bound on the error rate, state), and a full report is written every 7 days in which the rule was used.
15. Merge. A pull request holding only this tool's output for one batch, which passes the tool's verify check on the merge result, may be merged by the coordinating session. This is the only exception to the rule that count-changing pull requests need the owner's merge. Each merge is recorded in Kean with the count before and after.
16. Authority. The tool adopts only while a Kean decision that names this rule and the sha256 of this exact text is current. Changing any word or number needs a new decision.

```json
{"rule_id":"respondendi-v1","actions":["status_assignment.undecided","probe.status_assignment.undecided"],"statuses":["no","yes"],"yes_audit":"all","claims_per_control":15,"batch_max":30,"batches_per_day":1,"version_max":1000,"probation_clean_audits":59,"steady_audit_fraction":0.2,"steady_audit_min":2,"report_days":7,"auditor":["independent_ai_other_family","independent_human"]}
```
---

How each condition is machine-checked from pinned files:
- **1:** census CSV and ledger rows; `ADMISSION.json` (action in the list, order in `instrument_ids`); the action's strata file.
- **2 and 3:** the four bundle files named in `COMPLETION.json` `overlay_bundle`. Re-run the pure functions `status_overlay._decision_errors` and `_review_errors` (they need no repository state), check the proposal seal, `decision_sha256`, `review_sha256`, `evidence_sha256`, and `ready_for_owner_acceptance`.
- **4:** the member's line in both `BLIND_REVIEW_*.jsonl` files (or `AFTER_REVEAL_*.jsonl`), matched on `claim_sha256`; verdict, empty `defects`, `independent`, `separate_context`, `scope`; four distinct names.
- **5:** `COMPLETION.json` controls, seed receipts, a per-arm adjudication with `caught: true` and `scoring: strict`, and the planted hash rejected in the same two files. Where the planted claim is committed, the changed field paths (planted against genuine) must intersect the reviewer's defect `field`.
- **6:** `complete-vN/checker/PER_CLAIM.json` (`mechanical_result` pass, `gate_passed`, `all_checks_passed`, empty `gate_errors`), `RUN.json` returncode 0, `EXCEPTIONS.json` empty, `TALLY.json` outcome eligible, `PUBLICATION.json` `status_adoption_required` holds the order; then a live checker run on the staged canonical file.
- **7:** a scan of committed review records for the order through git objects (so a sparse checkout cannot hide one), excluding registered planted hashes; `SOURCE_AUDIT_HOLDS.jsonl`; the completion's `tracker-after/CONTESTED.csv`.
- **8:** re-hash every `text_path` in the claim and every `evidence.source_fingerprints` entry; the frozen ledger sha256 must be the hash of a line-boundary prefix of the current ledger, and the rows after it must not name the order.

proposals.name: Safeguards: seeded audit, stop rule, caps and owner report
proposals.design:
**Audit draw.** `draw_audit` seeds a random generator with sha256(rule sha256 + batch id + the sorted claim hashes), so the sample cannot be chosen by hand and can be re-derived by anyone.
- Probation (fewer than 59 agreeing audits in a row): every member.
- Steady state: ceil(0.2 x n), at least 2.
- Every YES, always.

**Audit before adoption.** The batch's rows are written only after its sampled audits are recorded and all agree. This avoids most reversals. The auditor gets the claim line, `EVIDENCE.json` and `DOSSIER.json` and the cited sources; it does not get `STATUS_REVIEW.json` or the blind reviews.

**Audit record** (`eo-standing-adoption-audit/v1`, one JSON line per order): `instrument_id`, `claim_sha256`, `auditor`, `auditor_role` (`independent_ai_other_family` or `independent_human`), `model_family`, `blind: true`, `status_supported`, `end_or_current_basis_supported`, `earlier_end_or_later_event_missed`, `verdict` (`agree` or `disagree`), `defects`, `started_utc`, `ended_utc`. The tool computes disagreement itself: either of the first two false, or the third true. For an AI auditor, `model_family` must differ from the manifest's `producer_model_family` and from every reviewer's `model_family`. A human audit is a status audit only; the row still says human-certified no.

**Stop rule.** On a disagreement, a control not caught by both arms, or a `verify` failure:
1. `suspend` appends a `suspended` event to `research/readiness/standing_adoption/STATE.jsonl` (hash-chained).
2. The batch is not adopted; its plan stays as evidence.
3. The tool prints the Kean ask to file.
4. Earlier adoptions from the same producer and reviewers are listed for a 100% audit; any found wrong is withdrawn.
5. The clean-audit run restarts at 0.
Anyone, including the tool, may suspend. Only an owner decision resumes: the `resumed` event must name a Kean decision whose ruling holds `resume=<sha256 of the suspension event>`.

**Caps.** 30 orders per batch, one batch per calendar day (UTC), 1,000 per rule version. `adopt` also refuses while the claim-kit lock holds reservations under an undecided action for orders outside the batch, unless `--allow-inflight` is given and recorded, because any ledger change stales their frozen evidence.

**Owner report.** `report` writes `research/readiness/standing_adoption/reports/<date>.md` and `.json`:
- per batch: orders, statuses, claim hashes, sample drawn, audit results;
- running totals: adopted, audited, disagreements, withdrawn;
- the 95% upper bound on the error rate from the current clean run, 1 - 0.05^(1/a), and the state.
It also prints the one-line text for the Kean brief. `adopt` refuses when more than 7 days of use have passed without a report.

**Kean.** Each adopted batch is one Kean finding with measures (attempted, submitted, filed; controls planted and missed) and the decided count before and after.

proposals.name: Owner-decision gate: no adoption without a Kean decision pinned to the rule's sha256
proposals.design:
`authority(repo)` is called first by `plan`, `adopt` and `verify`. It raises `Refused(code)` unless every step passes.

1. **Config.** `jobs/claim-kit/standing_adoption_rule.json` (`eo-standing-adoption-authority/v1`) names: `rule_text {path, sha256}`, `owner_ruling {path, sha256}`, `kean_decision_id`, `activation {path, sha256}`. It holds no parameters; those are read only from the hashed rule file.
2. **Rule hash.** sha256 of the rule file with CRLF normalised to LF (refuse a lone CR) equals `rule_text.sha256`. Code: `rule_text_changed`.
3. **Kean decision.** The highest revision of `kean_decision_id` in `jobs/kean/register/decisions.jsonl` exists, its `ruling` starts with `Owner:` and contains the literal `rule_sha256=<that hash>`, its `sources` include both paths, and it is `pinned`. Codes: `owner_decision_missing`, `owner_decision_hash_mismatch`.
4. **Ruling file.** Its sha256 matches and its text contains the same `rule_sha256=` token and the decision id.
5. **Activation receipt.** `research/readiness/standing_adoption/ACTIVATION.json` holds `pr_number`, `merge_commit`, `merged_by`, `rule_sha256`. The merge commit must be an ancestor of HEAD, and `git show <merge_commit>:<rule path>` must hash to the same value. `--online` also asks GitHub who merged that PR and compares it with `owner_login`.
6. **State.** Replay `STATE.jsonl` (each event carries `prev_sha256`): the last event must leave the rule `active`; a broken chain refuses.
7. **Limits.** Adopted count under this version below `version_max`.

No flag, environment variable or `--force` bypasses the gate; tests assert that.

Two further defences:
- `kean.py check` gains one rule: a decision whose ruling contains `rule_sha256=` must match the file in its sources. Editing the rule text without a new decision then fails the Kean check on every PR.
- `verify` runs in the daily chain-health job (Davy) and as a PR check, so a hand-added contract entry that claims the rule but lacks its record is caught.

Limit I could not design away: offline, the code can prove that the decision exists, that the hashes agree and that the activation commit is on main. It cannot prove a person merged it. That rests on the existing rule that PRs changing an owner ruling are owner-merged, plus the `--online` check.

- **Kean is writable by any agent.** `add-decision` takes any text, so an agent could write a matching decision. The activation receipt, the ancestry check and the online merged-by check narrow this; they do not close it for an agent with merge rights.
- **Line endings.** The Papinian adoption commit notes that validation was run on the committed LF bytes; a Windows checkout with CRLF conversion would change the hash, hence the normalisation.
- **Rigid token.** A reworded Kean ruling that drops the `rule_sha256=` token disables the rule until re-recorded. That fails safe.

proposals.design:
One module, clerical only: it selects, verifies, writes and reports. It makes no legal judgment and reads no reviewer reasons except the defect `field` names in condition 5.

**Functions**
```python

def authority(repo: Path, *, online: bool = False) -> dict
def state(repo: Path) -> dict             # status, clean_run, adopted, audited, disagreements, withdrawn
def candidates(repo: Path, completion_dir: Path) -> list[dict]
def check_member(repo: Path, completion_dir: Path, iid: str, auth: dict) -> dict
    # {'instrument_id','claim_sha256','status','checks': {name: {'ok','detail','pins'}}, 'qualifies'}
def rejection_scan(repo: Path, iid: str, planted: set[str]) -> list[dict]
def ledger_extends(repo: Path, frozen_sha256: str, iid: str) -> bool
def draw_audit(batch_id: str, members: list[dict], st: dict, params: dict) -> list[str]
def plan(repo: Path, completion_dirs: list[Path], batch_id: str) -> dict
def audit_packet(repo: Path, batch_id: str, dest: Path) -> dict
def record_audit(repo: Path, batch_id: str, audit_file: Path) -> dict
def adopt(repo: Path, batch_id: str, *, write: bool = False, allow_inflight: bool = False) -> dict
def withdraw(repo: Path, iid: str, *, reason_code: str, evidence: dict, decided_by: str, write: bool = False) -> dict
def suspend(repo: Path, reason: str, evidence: dict | None = None) -> dict
def resume(repo: Path, decision_id: str) -> dict
def verify(repo: Path, *, online: bool = False) -> dict
def report(repo: Path, *, since: str | None = None) -> dict
```

**CLI** (`python -I jobs/claim-kit/standing_adoption.py ...`)
- `authority [--online]`
- `plan BATCH_ID COMPLETE_DIR [COMPLETE_DIR ...]` writes `research/readiness/standing_adoption/batches/<id>/PLAN.json`: every member's checks, the pins and the audit draw. It changes nothing else.
- `audit-packet BATCH_ID --dest DIR` and `record-audit BATCH_ID FILE`
- `adopt BATCH_ID [--write]` (dry run by default)
- `withdraw EO:N --reason CODE --evidence PATH --decided-by NAME [--write]`
- `suspend --reason TEXT`, `resume --decision D-...`, `verify [--online]`, `report [--since DATE]`

**What `adopt --write` does**, in order:
1. `authority`; reload `PLAN.json`; re-run `check_member` for every member; require the sampled audits recorded and all agreeing.
2. Write `batches/<id>/ADOPTION_ROWS.csv` with the ledger's 19 columns, as in the Papinian rows. `decision_origin` is `respondendi-v1:<batch>:reviewed_claim <sha16> (status review + two-arm blind AI review + control; standing rule <decision id>; <rows path>)`; certified `no`.
3. Write `ADOPTION_RECORD.json` (rule sha256, decision id and revision, every member's pins and check results, audit pins).
4. Append the rows to the ledger in binary mode with LF.
5. Append one `accepted_additions` entry to `population_contract.json`: name, count, `accepted_in_main: "standing rule <decision id>"`, the rows pin, and `authorization_pins` for the rule text, the ruling, `ADOPTION_RECORD.json`, both blind files, after-reveal files, each `STATUS_REVIEW.json`, each `PUBLICATION.json` and the audit file.
6. File the canonical claims as `research/readiness/claims/<agent>-<date>-respondendi-<batch>.jsonl`, each line byte-identical to its `REPLACEMENT_PROPOSAL.jsonl` line (the whole file identical when every member is adopted, as in 936fa6ff55).
7. Run `population.validate_inputs` and the actual claim checker on the new file. On any failure restore the saved bytes of all four files from a journal and exit non-zero.
8. Append an `adopted` event to `STATE.jsonl`. It does not commit or push; the coordinator opens the PR.

**Tests** (`jobs/claim-kit/test_standing_adoption.py`, fixtures in the style of `test_population.py` and `test_overlay_completion.py`)
Authority:
1. Refuses with no config, and with no Kean decision.
2. Refuses when one byte of the rule text changes.
3. Refuses when the Kean ruling lacks the `rule_sha256=` token or carries another hash.
4. Accepts CRLF and LF copies of the same text; refuses a lone CR.
5. Refuses when suspended; `resume` needs a decision naming that suspension's hash.
6. Refuses on a broken `STATE.jsonl` chain.
7. No flag or environment variable bypasses any of these.
Member checks:
8. A real-shaped member passes all eight conditions.
9. Order already in the ledger: refused.
10. Missing admission receipt, or an action outside the list: refused.
11. Status review `reject`, or reviewer equal to producer: refused.
12. Arm B missing, arm B `rejected`, or arm B upheld a different hash: refused.
13. The same reviewer name on both arms: refused.
14. Control caught by one arm only: the whole review set is refused.
15. Fewer than one control per 15 claims: refused.
16. Control's genuine version without `upheld_after_reveal` from both arms: refused (the EO 11816 case).
17. Checker receipt missing, a failed step, or a non-empty `EXCEPTIONS.json`: refused.
18. A rejection of an earlier genuine version found in another wave folder: refused; a rejection of a registered planted hash is ignored.
19. Open source-audit hold on the claim hash: refused.
20. One source text byte changed since freezing: refused.
21. Ledger grew by other orders only: passes; ledger grew by this order, or its earlier bytes changed: refused.
22. YES without a CURRENT basis, or a YES not in the audit sample: refused.
Audit, caps, adoption:
23. `draw_audit` is deterministic, selects everything during probation and every YES always.
24. An AI auditor of the producer's family is refused; a human auditor is accepted and the row still says certified `no`.
25. A disagreement suspends, writes no ledger byte and resets the clean run.
26. A 31st member, a second batch the same day, or the version cap: refused.
27. After `adopt --write`, `validate_inputs` passes and the decided count rises by exactly the batch size; rows equal the pinned rows file in order.
28. The canonical lines are byte-identical to the proposal lines.
29. A failure injected at each write step leaves all four files byte-identical to the start.
30. `adopt` without `--write` changes no file.
Reversal and verify:
31. `withdraw` leaves `validate_inputs` passing with the count down by one; the original rows file is unchanged and still pinned.
32. The canonical claim line is unchanged and a hold line exists for its hash.
33. Withdrawing a row of the frozen historical baseline, or an order adopted by another route, is refused.
34. A withdrawn order can be adopted again by a later batch.
35. `verify` fails on a hand-added contract entry that names the rule without an `ADOPTION_RECORD.json`.

proposals.name: Reversal that keeps validate_inputs exact, plus three prerequisites
proposals.design:
**Reversal (works with today's `validate_inputs`, no change to population.py).** `validate_inputs` needs the ledger rows to equal the baseline plus each addition's pinned rows, in order, and forbids two rows for one order. A withdrawn row therefore has to leave both the ledger and the expected list. `withdraw` does this per batch:
1. Write `batches/<id>/ADOPTION_ROWS.r<k>.csv`: the batch's current rows minus the withdrawn row.
2. Write `batches/<id>/WITHDRAWAL_<EO_N>.json`: order, the withdrawn row's canonical sha256, reason code, evidence `{path, sha256}`, who decided, date.
3. In that batch's `accepted_additions` entry: point `rows` at the new file and lower `count` by one; add the original rows file and the withdrawal record to `authorization_pins`; add an informational `withdrawals` list.
4. Remove the row's line from the ledger (the frozen baseline prefix is untouched because it is pinned by byte length).
5. Append a line to `research/readiness/SOURCE_AUDIT_HOLDS.jsonl` (`eo-source-audit-hold/v1`, `state: unresolved`) for the claim hash, pointing at the withdrawal evidence. The tracker then blocks the order with `OPEN_SOURCE_AUDIT`. The canonical claim line stays, as `publication_audit` requires.
6. Run `validate_inputs`; restore on failure. Append a `withdrawn` event to `STATE.jsonl`.
Audit trail afterwards: the original rows file is byte-identical and still hash-pinned in the contract, the withdrawal record is pinned, and the claim and its hold are visible. Only Respondendi's own batches can be withdrawn this way.

**Cleaner follow-on (needs a rebuild).** Add `accepted_withdrawals` to the contract and to `validate_inputs`: each entry pins a withdrawal CSV and an `applies_after_addition` index; the matching row (exactly one, hash-matched, never from the baseline) is removed from the expected list, and the result reports `authorized_withdrawals`. `population.py` is in `COMPILER_FILES`, so this edit stales every frozen evidence and compiled output until claim-kit rebuilds; land it between waves.

**Prerequisite 1: both arms and the control in the record.** The successor to `overlay_review.py` should (a) write one control adjudication per arm, each pinning that arm's review line, and (b) commit the planted claim versions after review as `reviews/PLANTED_CONTROLS.jsonl`. Then condition 5 is checked by field-path comparison instead of the present word match on "date", "year" and similar. It should also give every control an after-reveal review in the same wave; u01b did not, which is why EO 11816 was never reviewed.

**Prerequisite 2: admission receipt v2.** `admission.record` should add `plan_sha256` and `strata_sha256` so condition 1 is checkable from pins. `admission.py` is not in `COMPILER_FILES`.

**Prerequisite 3: plan around the ledger pin.** Frozen overlay evidence pins the whole ledger file, so each adoption stales in-flight undecided bundles. Short term the adopter refuses while such reservations are open. Longer term `status_overlay` could accept a ledger that extends the frozen one by other orders' rows; `status_overlay.py` is not in `COMPILER_FILES`, but `completion.working_overlay` re-pins the same hash and would need the same change.

- **Editing an accepted entry.** The no-code reversal changes `rows` and `count` in an existing `accepted_additions` entry, which the contract's purpose line describes as frozen. The original stays pinned, but the owner may prefer the explicit `accepted_withdrawals` route despite the rebuild.
- **Claim on an undecided order.** I confirmed that an open hold blocks readiness; I did not confirm how the tracker treats a canonical claim whose order has no ledger status and no hold, so the hold must never be skipped.
- **Hold file format.** A hold needs a `review_path` whose bytes match `review_sha256`, or the tracker raises; the withdrawal record serves as that file.
- **Prerequisite 3's longer-term change** loosens a staleness check in the status handoff and needs its own review.

design:redteam-throughput.summary:

WHAT I ATTACKED. The draft rule already exists in the worktree: C:/Users/danie/eo-wt/respondendi/jobs/respondendi-adoption/RULE.md (v1, NO only, status-only clause 7, 34% probation audit by another family until 59 agreeing audits in a row, one disagreement stops) with C:/Users/danie/eo-wt/respondendi/jobs/respondendi-adoption/respondendi.py. Verdict: the rule's shape is sound (pinned trail, reversal, caps, audit debt) but as written it does not bound the error rate it claims to bound, and its stop rule will probably cost the owner more decisions than per-lot approval. It becomes defensible if restricted to one deterministic lot and given a real audit plan.

RED TEAM FINDINGS (each with measured basis)
1. Common-mode evidence, not just common model family. Producer (Sonnet), status reviewer and both arms (Opus) are all Anthropic, and the reviewer prompt (tools/prompts/reviewer_overlay.txt) confines both arms to the same frozen EVIDENCE.json/DOSSIER.json plus sources the claim cites. The diagnosis shows the dossier itself is wrong in ways all three share: 'current-law:usc 0 hits' false for at least 9 orders (10195, 10771, 10917, 11053, 11118, 11575, 13024, 13552, 14198), a neighbour order's body as the sole clause (7573), inverted ACT edges (12379), misattributed actors (13329, 10624). Kean F-20261107-septuagint-xfamily: Claude arms caught 17/22 plants, Codex 8/8, and the removed-later-event plant was missed by every reviewer of BOTH families. So a different family helps on commission errors and does not help on omission errors. Same-family instability on rule questions is measured in this diagnosis: the refuter flipped the best status of 6 of 90 orders (6.7%; 7721, 9680, 10917, 14223, 11315, 13013), 5 of the 6 on doctrine (wind-up directions, report-order residue, amend-only P2). A reviewer also injected an error (EO 10816) that the coordinator relayed.
2. Controls are too easy and too few. tools/review_prep.py plants one defect type: every end date minus three years, detectable by comparing the claim's date with the quoted source. It never tests the defects that flip a status: partial revocation read as whole, transfer read as an end (EO 8875), a revoker that was later undone, an omitted savings clause or later event, wrong-order text. On this route there are 3 controls in total (3/3 caught: 95% lower bound on catch rate 37%); wave-wide 18/18 gives 85% but for that one plant type. Dorotheus Sonnet arms: 25/30. RULE.md condition 5 counts controls, not kinds; control picks are seeded by batch name, so the coordinator that briefs the arms can know them.
3. Goodhart is already observed. status_overlay.py:684 checks only that a basis id starts with ACT:/TERM:/ACTOR_TEXT:. EO 9680's producer cited the creating order to satisfy it (caught by the status reviewer); EO 12379's inverted ACT records would have passed mechanically. The rule allows only NO, Bentham scores filed per attempt, UNDECIDED_CHECKLIST.md item 11 says never leave a status decision unreviewed, and nothing caps resubmissions, so pressure runs unknown -> NO and reject -> resubmit until two arms uphold.
4. Scale changes the population. All 16 adoptions so far are the easiest class (named revocation in a held text). RULE.md has no class restriction (allowed_actions is the whole stratum), and clause 7 (status-only in partial_research scope) has never been run: 0 reviews and 0 controls in that scope. Once kit fixes admit own-terms, amend-only, authority-repeal and pre-1937 working-text cases, they flow in under the same rule hash with no new bound. The project is not uniform on amend-only orders (EO 12043 is provisional YES; P2 says spent on issue).
5. The audit statistics do not hold. (a) '59 agreeing in a row' restarts after a failure, so a process with a 5% error rate passes eventually with probability 1; the exit test must be cumulative. (b) 34% of a 60-order lot cannot bound that lot: 21 audits miss all of 3 errors 27% of the time; bounding a 60-lot at 5% needs 31-38 audits. Only a pooled, stationary process bound is feasible, which needs fixed strata and a pinned process. (c) 59 clean audits detect a true 5% rate 95% of the time but a 2% rate only 70% and 1% only 45%. (d) The sample seed is the lot's own core hash (respondendi.py:626-630), computable before writing and steerable by lot composition. (e) Auditor name and model family are self-declared strings (respondendi.py:727).
6. The stop rule has no adjudication. One disagreement stops everything and needs an owner resume decision. The only measured cross-family non-uphold rate on Claude-upheld statuses is Sinclair 2/31 (6.5%, 95% 0.8-21%). At 5% the chance of 59 clean audits is 4.8% and the expected number of audits to leave probation is about 390 (about 800 at 6.5%), so probation never ends and each false alarm costs an owner decision.
7. An audit on held sources measures agreement, not truth. Errors caused by an instrument nobody holds (reinstatement, PLO, unnamed statute) are invisible to producer, arms and auditor alike. Only an outside-source check breaks that.
8. Drift is unpinned. The RULE.md hash pins the rule text only; prompts, checklist, claim-kit code, checker and model ids can change without a new decision. Separately, frozen evidence pins whole-file hashes of the census and status tables (status_overlay.py:75-101, 559-560), so every automatic adoption invalidates every undecided batch in flight (stale_authority_snapshot).

AUDIT SIZE AND STOP RULE (exact binomial, one-sided 95%)
Zero confirmed errors: 29 audits -> 10%, 59 -> 4.95% (the Jacquard figure), 99 -> 3%, 149 -> 2%, 299 -> 1%. With confirmed errors, a 5% bound needs 93 audits for 1 error, 124 for 2, 153 for 3. For a finite lot of about 940, 56 clean audits give 5%. Recommended: per stratum, audit the first 59 adoptions in full before the rule runs unattended; a disagreement goes to adjudication; a confirmed error reverses the order, stops the stratum and extends the plan to the next row of the table; two confirmed errors within 59 end the stratum's standing adoption until the owner re-approves. A 5% bound on about 855 adoptions still tolerates about 43 wrong statuses; 2% needs 149 clean audits. That tolerance is the owner's choice.

proposals.name: Wald audit plan: front-loaded, cumulative, adjudicated, per stratum
proposals.kind: safeguard (audit sample size and stop rule)
proposals.design: Named for Abraham Wald, who founded sequential analysis. Replace 'probation until 59 agreeing audits in a row' and '34% of each lot'. Per stratum (lot id x process fingerprint): (1) the first 59 adopted orders are all audited by a different model family or a person, and no further lot is adopted until they are; 59 with zero confirmed errors gives a 4.95% one-sided 95% bound (D-20261031-jacquard); for a finite lot of about 940, 56 suffice. (2) A disagreement is not a stop: it goes to adjudication by a third reviewer of another kind or the owner within a fixed time; only a confirmed error counts. (3) Each confirmed error reverses the order, triggers a full audit of that lot, and extends the plan: 93 audits for 1 error, 124 for 2, 153 for 3 to keep the 5% bound. (4) Two confirmed errors within any 59 audits, or a cumulative bound above 10% after 30 audits, ends standing adoption for the stratum until the owner re-approves. (5) After the plan is met, 10% surveillance, and the report prints the cumulative bound per stratum, never a streak. (6) The sample is drawn by a seed the adopting session cannot choose, for example the merge commit hash of the adoption PR, drawn in CI. (7) The audit record pins the auditor's transcript or run id so family and identity are evidence, not a typed string. (8) Each quarter the owner or another person checks 10 audited-agree orders against an outside source (govinfo or the Federal Register site), which is the only check that can see a missing instrument.

proposals.name: Semantic basis check and outlier screens before any standing adoption
proposals.design: Zero-token checks run on every proposal before review and again at adoption. Basis: the cited ACT or ACTOR_TEXT span must contain the target's number within the same sentence as an ending verb, the acting instrument must be dated after the target, and the claimed end date must equal the acting instrument's signing or stated effective date. Also cap resubmissions at one, with fresh arms, and put every resubmitted claim in the audit sample.

proposals.name: Harrison pin: process fingerprint and adoption at wave boundaries
proposals.design: Named for John Harrison, whose chronometers made drift measurable. Each lot receipt pins a process fingerprint: SHA-256 of the producer and reviewer prompts and checklist, the claim-kit compiler fingerprint, the checker version, the control catalogue and the model ids of producer, status reviewer and arms. A changed fingerprint opens a new stratum whose first 59 adoptions are audited in full again; a pure bug fix can be exempted only by a recorded owner decision. Separately, standing adoption writes to the status table only at a wave boundary (one adoption commit a day, after in-flight batches complete), because frozen evidence pins whole-file hashes of the census and status tables and every append raises stale_authority_snapshot for batches in flight; longer term, pin the order's own authority row instead of the whole file.

proposals.name: Campbell monitors: watch the pressure the yield metric creates
proposals.design: Named for Campbell's law. The owner report adds, per wave and per producer: the share of readings that are no, yes and unknown against the measured baseline (Papinian producers 47/14/29 of 90; diagnosis 56/15/19); the share of proposals resting on each basis kind; resubmission counts; the status-reviewer rejection rate (2 of 24 so far); arm disagreement on genuine claims (EO 10938: one arm upheld, one rejected); and control catch rates by kind. A shift of the no share or a fall of the unknown share beyond the baseline's 95% interval puts the wave's adoptions into full audit. Bentham counts an undecided adoption as filed only after its audit agrees or its audit window closes, so the gate does not reward unaudited volume. Producers are scored on blocker accuracy as well: a sample of blocked orders is re-read each wave (this diagnosis found producers' 'not held' statements wrong or incomplete in about a third of blocked orders).
